# Requirements Document

## Introduction

A diagram opens as two correlated one-way legs: `Open` streams a baseline and then every later change, and `UpdateView` is the unary call telling the backend what the client can currently see. The backend answers a view report with the deltas that bring the connection into line. This is the **view-delta mechanism**, and mindmap is its reference implementation.

**Scope is universal and settled by the user: every diagram module implements it.** This document states no criterion for which modules qualify and argues no exclusions.

**What the mechanism is, in the user's own words:** *"when panning/zooming the map the deltas should be used to update the client accordingly."* That is a **behavioural** definition and it is sharper than any structural one, because it makes the feature a live loop rather than a report at open: a pan or a zoom changes what the reader can see, the client reports the new viewport, and the backend answers with deltas for what has come into view. A module that reports its viewport once when the diagram opens has not implemented this. It has implemented the first frame of it.

**Measured against that definition, the tree divides in three.** Reference counts do not settle it — what settles it is whether a view *change* re-fires the report, which means looking at the effect that calls it and what it is keyed on.

| | Modules | What was found |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **The loop works** | mindmap, c4, azure-pipeline, ansible-structure | A debounced effect keyed on the view (`[viewKey, loading, failed]`, or the view box's own fields) calls `reportView` on every settled change, and the backend's `UpdateView` answers with real deltas. Panning and zooming genuinely update the client. |
| **Reports once, not adopted** | *(none)* | Looked for specifically, and the category is **empty**: every module that reports at all reports on view change. |
| **Never reports** | timeline, dependency-graph, wardley-map, helm-charts, databricks, rdf, sparql | No client report and `UpdateView` returning `[]`. **Five of the seven state a reason** — timeline (`TimelineSession.cs`), dependency-graph (`DependencyGraphSession.cs`) and wardley-map (`WardleySession.cs`) at the method, e.g. *"the connection already holds the whole timeline, and the view transform is the client's own"*; helm-charts (`HelmSession.cs`) and databricks (`DatabricksSession.cs`) in their class remarks, e.g. *"a bounded diagram of tens of elements has nothing to virtualize"*. **rdf (`Owl/OwlSession.cs`) returns `[]` with no stated reason**, and sparql has no canvas at all. Every path is under `src/diagrams/<module>/backend/`, so the count can be checked as quickly as it was made. |

So the gap is **seven modules**, and it is a real gap under the user's definition: in all seven, panning and zooming produce no deltas at all. Six of them declined the mechanism deliberately when their element counts were small, which was a reasonable local judgement and is now superseded — the user has decided the loop belongs everywhere, and a module that declines it stays correct only for as long as its documents stay small. `rdf` is the case where the cost is already visible: it opens documents of more than 1,600 resources and carries a first-N truncation banner *because* it has no viewport filtering, which is a strictly worse answer to the same problem — it discards by document order rather than by what the reader is looking at, so panning never recovers the rest.

**With scope settled, centralization is the whole substance — and the duplication is larger than a single function.** Three separate pieces are copied across the four working modules:

1. **`reportView`** — the hook function that builds the `UpdateView` request. The four copies are **character-identical**: the same centre-and-bounding-box arithmetic, the same correlation fields, the same deliberately swallowed rejection.
2. **The debounced effect** — every canvas carries its own `const VIEW_REPORT_DEBOUNCE_MS = 200`, its own `reportViewRef`, and the same `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` effect. mindmap's and c4's are character-identical, down to the dependency array.
3. **`shownRectOf`** — the conversion from the canvas's view box to a viewport rectangle, defined privately three times. mindmap's and c4's are identical two-argument versions; azure-pipeline's is a one-argument variant that needs no surface element.

Eleven modules times three copied pieces is the outcome this repository has already produced twice — pan and drag state hand-rolled across ten canvases, readers duplicated across eleven stores. Doing it a third time knowingly would be worse than doing it twice by accident.

**Three specifications now touch the same viewport state, and Requirement 6 states the seam once rather than leaving it to be discovered three times.** [`drag-and-drop-centralization`](../drag-and-drop-centralization/requirements.md) owns **pan** as one of its five gesture derivatives; [`canvas-scrollbars`](../canvas-scrollbars/requirements.md) makes a scrollbar thumb another way to pan and requires the thumb to follow a pan by any means; and this specification requires any change to the view — by either of those or by zoom — to produce a view report. The three are compatible because each attaches to one thing: the canvas's own view state.

**Protocol history constrains the shape and nothing here changes it.** `diagrams.proto` records that this service was first declared as a bidirectional Connect stream and was split because a browser on grpc-web cannot stream a request body. `UpdateView` is a unary call correlated to the stream by `watch_id` and path, and that pairing is load-bearing.

## Alignment with Product Vision

* [product.md](../../steering/product.md)'s **"Live, pushed updates"** — this is the mechanism by which what a reader can see stays true as they move around it.
* product.md's **"Value from day one"** — a reader who opens a 1,600-resource ontology should see the part they are looking at, not the first thousand things in file order.
* [tech.md](../../steering/tech.md)'s **gRPC call shapes** — the paired-leg design is settled; this spec adopts it further rather than renegotiating it.
* [structure.md](../../steering/structure.md)'s **core-vs-module boundary** — what is identical across modules moves to the shared client library; what is genuinely each module's own stays in the module.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1 — Every diagram module implements the loop

**User Story:** As a reader of any diagram, I want panning and zooming to bring me the content I have moved to, so that a large document is as usable as a small one.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN any diagram module is open THEN panning or zooming SHALL cause the client to report the new viewport, and the backend SHALL answer with the deltas that bring the connection into line.
2. WHEN this specification completes THEN **all eleven diagram modules** SHALL implement the loop — the four that already do, and the seven that do not: timeline, dependency-graph, wardley-map, helm-charts, databricks, rdf and sparql.
3. WHEN a module is judged complete THEN the test SHALL be behavioural, per the user's definition: **a view change produces deltas**. A module that reports its viewport only at open SHALL NOT count as having implemented this, and neither SHALL one whose `UpdateView` returns `[]` regardless of the viewport it was given.
4. WHEN a module's backend answers a view report THEN it SHALL send what has come into view and MAY take back what has left, so that the connection's contents follow the reader rather than growing without bound.
5. WHEN `sparql` gains its canvas — it has none today, only `api/` and `backend/` — THEN it SHALL implement the loop at that point rather than joining a later catch-up.

### Requirement 2 — What "just like mindmap" means, split into mechanism and mindmap's own

**User Story:** As an implementer, I want to know which parts of the reference implementation to copy and which are mindmap's business, so that I neither reinvent the mechanism nor inherit somebody else's semantics.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the reference is read THEN these SHALL be treated as **the mechanism**, and centralized per Requirement 3: building the `UpdateView` request from a viewport rectangle; the correlation fields; treating a failed report as advisory and swallowing it; debouncing so a pan costs one report per settle rather than one per frame; and re-reporting whenever the view changes.
2. WHEN the reference is read THEN these SHALL be treated as **mindmap's own** and SHALL NOT be centralized: what its elements are, how it decides which of them the viewport intersects, what its `UpdateView` does with its document store, and how its canvas derives a view box from its own units.
3. WHEN a module adopts the mechanism THEN it SHALL supply only its own viewport rectangle and its own visibility decision, and SHALL restate none of Requirement 2.1's parts.
4. WHEN the split is disputed for a specific piece THEN the test SHALL be whether it mentions any module's domain: a piece that names elements, nodes, stages, rows or resources is the module's; a piece that speaks only of rectangles, paths and watch ids is the mechanism's.

### Requirement 3 — One implementation of the client half

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want the view report written once, so that eleven modules do not carry eleven copies of it.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the client half is centralized THEN it SHALL live in the shared client diagram library beside `useDiagramStream`, and SHALL cover all three duplicated pieces: the request builder, the debounced re-report on view change, and the view-box-to-rectangle conversion.
2. WHEN the four existing copies are replaced THEN no module SHALL retain its own `reportView`, its own `VIEW_REPORT_DEBOUNCE_MS`, or its own private `shownRectOf`.
3. WHEN the conversion is centralized THEN it SHALL accommodate the one genuine variant found — azure-pipeline's needs no surface element where mindmap's and c4's take one — either by making the surface optional or by keeping two named conversions, and SHALL NOT force a caller to pass an argument it has no use for.
4. WHEN a module supplies its viewport THEN it SHALL do so in its own canvas units, and the shared code SHALL perform no unit conversion of its own.
5. WHEN the centralization lands THEN no module client SHALL construct an `updateView` request itself, and a guard SHALL fail naming any module that does — the discipline the drag-and-drop and scrollbar specs apply, for the same reason: copied client plumbing spreads silently.
6. **Adopting the shared report SHALL NOT require adopting `useDiagramStream`**, so that this specification does not become a larger migration wearing a smaller name — three of the eleven modules hand-roll their open loop, and changing that is not in scope here.

### Requirement 4 — The backend halves are judged on behaviour, not resemblance

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want the centralization to stop where the similarity stops, so that it does not merge different things into one that fits none of them.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the four existing backend `UpdateView` implementations are compared THEN they SHALL be treated as **genuinely different**: c4 diffs two visible-element sets inline, ansible-structure delegates to its element mapper's `Diff`, azure-pipeline diffs over expansion state as well as viewport, and mindmap consults its document store first. They resemble each other only in returning deltas.
2. WHEN a shared backend helper is proposed THEN it SHALL be justified by three or more consumers wanting **the same behaviour**, not by consumers whose code merely rhymes.
3. IF a genuine common piece emerges once seven more modules implement the loop — the likeliest candidate being "diff a previously delivered set against a currently visible one and emit Remove-then-Add" — THEN it MAY be centralized on that evidence, and modules whose behaviour differs SHALL keep their own.
4. WHEN this specification completes THEN the backend implementations SHALL NOT have been merged merely to raise the count of things centralized.

### Requirement 5 — Adopting the loop changes nothing a reader already relies on

**User Story:** As a user of any of these diagrams, I want this to be invisible except that large diagrams get better.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a module that already works adopts the shared client code THEN its behaviour SHALL be unchanged: the same reports at the same moments with the same contents, and its existing tests SHALL pass unchanged.
2. WHEN a module that has never reported adopts the loop THEN everything the reader can currently do SHALL still work, and no element visible before SHALL disappear except by leaving the viewport.
3. WHEN a small document is opened THEN the loop SHALL cost no visible behaviour change: a diagram whose whole content fits the view reports its viewport and receives nothing further, which is correct rather than wasteful.
4. WHEN a module's `UpdateView` becomes viewport-aware THEN its truncation or budget mechanism, where it has one, SHALL be re-evaluated against it: a budget SHALL remain as a floor against a pathological view but SHALL NOT be the primary means of keeping a large document drawable.
5. WHEN `diagrams.proto` is considered THEN it SHALL NOT change.

### Requirement 6 — Where the three viewport specifications meet

**User Story:** As a maintainer of three specs that touch one piece of state, I want the seam stated once, so that none of them quietly undoes another.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. **The canvas's own view state is the single source of truth**, and all three specifications attach to it rather than owning it: `drag-and-drop-centralization`'s **pan** derivative writes it, `canvas-scrollbars`' thumb writes it and reads it back to place the thumb, and this specification reports it after it settles.
2. WHEN the view changes by any means — pan gesture, scrollbar thumb, wheel zoom, a programmatic reveal — THEN the report of Requirement 1.1 SHALL fire, so that adoption is not silently partial for one of the ways a view can move.
3. WHEN `canvas-scrollbars` is implemented THEN its requirement that the thumb follows a pan by any means and this specification's requirement that any view change is reported SHALL be satisfied by the same state change, not by two mechanisms observing each other.
4. WHEN `drag-and-drop-centralization` centralizes the pan gesture THEN the report SHALL remain a consequence of the resulting view change rather than being wired into the gesture, so that a view change from a source that is not a gesture still reports.
5. WHENEVER these three specifications disagree in detail THEN the ordering above SHALL settle it: state is the module's, gestures write it, scrollbars write and read it, and reporting observes it.

### Requirement 7 — The mechanism is documented where the next module will look

**User Story:** As the author of the next diagram module, I want to know that this loop is expected and how to wire it, before I have written a truncation instead.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the work completes THEN `docs/creating-a-diagram-module.md` SHALL describe the loop, state that every module implements it, and show the shared client code in use.
2. WHEN it is documented THEN the behavioural test of Requirement 1.3 SHALL be stated: a view change produces deltas, and a report only at open is not adoption.
3. WHEN the shared code is added THEN the shared client library's readme SHALL name it beside the pieces already there.

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Code Architecture and Modularity

- One implementation of the client half, shared; each module supplies its viewport rectangle and its own visibility decision.
- No shared backend implementation without three consumers wanting the same behaviour.

### Performance

- Reports SHALL remain debounced, so a pan costs one report per settle rather than one per animation frame.
- Adopting the loop in a large-document module SHALL reduce the elements delivered, that being the point; in a small-document module it SHALL add one unary call per settled view change and nothing else.

### Reliability

- A failed view report SHALL never surface as an error to the reader: the backend keeps the last window it had, which is what all four current copies already do.
- A module mid-adoption SHALL remain correct: delivering the whole diagram at baseline and answering `[]` is consistent, so partially-migrated trees never show a broken diagram.
